statement.p: Let \vec r=x\,\vec i+y\,\vec j+z\,\vec k and \vec a = 2\,\vec i + 6\,\vec j + \,\vec k.
(b) Let C be a path from the origin to the point with position vector \vec{r_0} = a\,\vec i + b\,\vec j + c\,\vec k. Find \int_C\nabla(\vec r\cdot\vec a)\cdot d\vec r.
(c) If \|\vec r_0\|=14, what is the maximum possible value of \int_C\nabla(\vec r\cdot\vec a)\cdot d\vec r? (Be sure you can explain why your answer is correct.)
maximum value of \int_C\nabla(\vec r\cdot\vec a)\cdot d\vec r =

solution.p: (a) Since \vec r\cdot\vec a = 2 x + 6 y + z, we have \nabla(\vec r\cdot \vec a) = 2 \, \vec i + 6 \, \vec j + \, \vec k=\vec a.
(b) By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals, we have \int_C\nabla(\vec r\cdot \vec a)\cdot d\vec r = \vec r\cdot \vec a\bigg|_{(0,0,0)}^{(a,b,c)} = \vec r_0\cdot \vec a = 2 a + 6 b + c.

(c) Since \vec r_0\cdot \vec a=\|\vec r_0\| \|\vec a\|\cos\theta = 14\|\vec a\|\cos\theta, where \theta is the angle between \vec r_0 and \vec a, the maximum value of \vec r_0\cdot\vec a occurs if \vec r_0 is parallel to \vec a. Then \theta=0 and \int_C\nabla(\vec r\cdot\vec a)\cdot d\vec r = 14 \|\vec a\|\cos 0 = 14\sqrt{2^2 + 6^2 + 1^2} = 14\sqrt{41}.
